figures.caption: 圖一：評分 4.9 的熱門餐廳
figures.description: 一家裝潢新穎的餐廳，招牌上寫著網路評分「★ 4.9（2,358 則評論）」。門口排著長長的隊伍，一直延伸到人行道上，排隊的人幾乎都低頭看著手機，有人在看餐點的照片。

figures.label: 圖二
figures.caption: 圖二：隔壁評論很少的老麵店
figures.description: 就在圖一餐廳的隔壁，一家老麵店的招牌寫著「★ 4.6（8 則評論）」，網路上的評論很少。店裡的湯鍋冒著熱氣，桌椅擺得整整齊齊，卻一個客人也沒有；年老的老闆獨自坐在門邊，望著隔壁排隊的人潮。

questions.stem: 提示：現在許多人決定去哪裡吃飯、買什麼東西之前，都會先上網查看評分與評論。請仔細觀察下面兩張圖，寫一篇英文作文，文分兩段。第一段比較圖一與圖二兩家店的情形；第二段說明網路評價為什麼能左右人們的選擇，評估這個現象對消費者與店家的影響，並提出你自己參考網路評價時會採取的做法。

1.explanation_zh: 這一題第一段比較兩家店；第二段有三項任務：網路評價為什麼能左右選擇、對消費者與店家的影響、自己參考評價的做法。圖中兩家店就在隔壁，差別在評分與評論數，第一段要把這個關鍵點出來。第二段最好寫出「評論多、客人多、評論更多」的循環，並同時評估對消費者與店家的影響；做法要具體，只寫「不要盲目相信評價」太空泛。
evidence: 比較圖一與圖二兩家店的情形
說明網路評價為什麼能左右人們的選擇
評估這個現象對消費者與店家的影響
提出你自己參考網路評價時會採取的做法
1.strategy_zh: 第二段先用一兩句說明原因，再用因果循環寫影響，接著用自己被評價誤導的經驗帶出做法；做法寫成兩三個具體的習慣。
hints: 第一段：比較評分、評論數與店門口的景象，最後點出差異的關鍵
第二段前半：評價為什麼有影響力，以及對消費者、店家的正反影響
第二段後半：用自己的經驗帶出參考評價的具體做法，最後寫出見解

content.focus_zh: 第一段要比較兩家店的情形（評分與評論數、排隊與空店、顧客與老闆的動作），並點出差異的關鍵；第二段要說明網路評價影響選擇的原因，評估對消費者與店家的正反影響，再提出自己參考評價的具體做法。

bands.descriptor_zh: 回應題目的每一項要求，主旨明確；用具體的事例、細節或親身經驗撐起每個重點。
大致回應題目，但有一項要求寫得單薄，或細節偏籠統、說服力不足。
漏掉題目的主要要求或主旨模糊，多數句子空泛、重複或偏離題目。
空白、離題、只抄題目，或內容少到無法判斷要說什麼。

organization.focus_zh: 第二段任務多，要依「原因、影響、做法」推進；影響最好寫成因果循環（評論多、客人多、評論更多），讓推論有層次。

bands.descriptor_zh: 兩段分工清楚，各有主題句；句與句、段與段的銜接自然，轉承語用得恰當，篇幅分配合理。
段落大致分明，但有的地方跳接或重複，轉承語偏少或用得生硬。
重點排列混亂，前後句常接不起來，讀者不容易跟上。
看不出段落與順序，句子彼此無關。

grammar.focus_zh: 比較可用 while、whereas、by contrast；說明原因可用分詞片語（Faced with…）；寫影響與做法時注意主詞動詞一致與平行結構。

bands.descriptor_zh: 句子幾乎沒有文法、標點錯誤，能交替使用簡單句、複句與不同的句首。
偶有時態、單複數或標點錯誤，但讀得懂意思；句型變化有限。
錯誤多到常讓人誤解意思，句子結構常不完整。
幾乎沒有正確的句子，無法理解。

vocabulary.focus_zh: 評價相關字詞要精確（rating、review、comment、fake、customer），避免一直重複 good、many。

bands.descriptor_zh: 用字精準、貼切，搭配自然，少有重複；拼字與大小寫幾乎全對。
字彙範圍偏窄、常重複同幾個字，偶有用字不當或拼錯，但不妨礙理解。
用錯字或拼錯字很多，常讓人看不懂。
幾乎每個字都用錯或拼錯，無法理解。

rubric.deductions_zh: 字數明顯不足（少於 100 個單詞）或沒有分成兩段，各扣總分 1 分；兩種情形同時發生只扣 1 分。離題或空白以 0 分計。

checklist_zh: 第一段有沒有用圖中的細節（評分、評論數、排隊、空店）比較兩家店，並點出差異的關鍵
第二段有沒有說明評價為什麼有影響力（省時間、降低風險、跟著多數人選）
影響是否兼顧消費者與店家，而且正反兩面都有
自己的做法是否具體（看什麼、忽略什麼、多久做一次），結尾是否提出見解

model_texts.label: steady
model_texts.text:
The two pictures show two restaurants on the same street. In Picture 1, a restaurant with a rating of 4.9 stars has a long line outside. Many people are looking at their phones while they wait. In Picture 2, however, the old noodle shop next door is almost empty. It has only a few online reviews, and the owner is sitting alone and looking at the crowd next door. Although the two shops are very close, their business is completely different.
Online reviews affect people's choices because they are quick and easy to read. When we visit a new place, we want to avoid bad food, so we trust what other customers say. This habit can help us find good places, but it also has problems. Some reviews are fake, and popular shops are not always better. For example, last month my friends and I waited an hour to get into a famous dessert shop, but the cake was just ordinary. Meanwhile, small shops without many reviews may lose customers and even close. Therefore, when I read reviews, I check the comments instead of only the stars, and I sometimes try a shop that has few reviews. After all, my own taste is the best judge.

paragraphs.function_zh: 比較兩張圖：高評分餐廳大排長龍，隔壁評論很少的老麵店空無一人，最後點出兩家店距離近、生意卻差很多

paragraphs.function_zh: 原因＋評估＋提出方案：評價好讀又能避開地雷，但有假評論、小店也會受害（附排隊吃甜點的經驗），再提出看留言、試小店的做法

model_texts.label: top
model_texts.text:
The two pictures capture how a single number can divide the fortunes of two neighbors. In the first, customers stretch far down the sidewalk outside a trendy restaurant whose sign proudly displays a 4.9-star rating, and many of them are scrolling through photos of its dishes while they wait. Right next door, by contrast, an old noodle shop with only a handful of online reviews sits almost empty, its owner gazing at the crowd that never comes inside. Steam is still rising from his pots, but every table is empty. Although the two shops share a wall, they seem to belong to different worlds. The food in both places may be equally good, yet one is overwhelmed while the other is overlooked. What separates them, it seems, is not the quality of their cooking but their visibility on the Internet.
Online ratings carry such power because they promise to save us time and protect us from risk. Faced with dozens of unfamiliar choices, people naturally trust hundreds of strangers more than their own guesses. This habit does help consumers avoid truly bad service, and it pushes businesses to improve. However, it also creates a cycle that favors the already popular: a crowded shop attracts more reviews, more reviews attract more customers, and quieter shops, such as family businesses run by older owners who rarely use social media, slowly disappear. Worse still, some shops manipulate their ratings with paid or fake reviews, which damages the credibility of the whole system. I learned this the hard way last month, when my friends and I queued for over an hour at a famous dessert café, only to be served a cake that tasted no different from one at a convenience store. Meanwhile, a family-run bakery near my home, which has fewer than twenty reviews, makes the best pineapple cakes I have ever eaten. Since then, I have treated ratings as a starting point rather than a final verdict. I now read the most recent comments in detail, ignore extreme ones, and, once a month, deliberately try a place with few reviews. If more people did the same, our streets would remain diverse, and our choices would truly be our own.

paragraphs.function_zh: 比較兩張圖：用排隊、滑手機、冒熱氣的空店與老闆的眼神對照兩家店，最後點出差別在網路能見度而不是料理
paragraphs.topic_sentence: The two pictures capture how a single number can divide the fortunes of two neighbors.

paragraphs.function_zh: 原因＋評估＋提出方案：說明評價省時、降風險的力量，用「評論多、客人多」的循環評估對店家的衝擊與假評論問題，以親身經驗帶出三個具體做法與見解
paragraphs.topic_sentence: Online ratings carry such power because they promise to save us time and protect us from risk.

self_assessment.explanation_zh: 第一段用細節比較並點出差異的關鍵，第二段說明原因、用因果循環評估對店家的衝擊與假評論問題，再以正反兩個經驗帶出具體做法與見解（內容 5）；任務依序推進，轉承語清楚（組織 5）；獨立分詞構句、what 子句、only to V、假設語氣正確多樣（文法句構 5）；用字精準（overwhelmed、overlooked、visibility、verdict），仍以常用字為主（字彙拼字 4）。總分 19，屬頂標版。

top.comment_zh: 第一段對照排隊人潮與空店、老闆望著隔壁的動作，點出差異關鍵是網路能見度而非手藝；評論數只寫 a handful，沒寫兩家的星等差與 2,358 則，但重點清楚。第二段說明網路評價的吸引力（Faced with… 分詞構句），寫出「人多、評論多、客人更多」的循環與假評論，用排隊吃甜點失望與住家附近麵包店的經驗帶出三項具體做法，結尾有見解。

steady.comment_zh: 第一段比較評分、排隊與空店、老闆的動作；第二段說明網路評價方便、想避開難吃的店，評估假評論與小店可能倒閉，以甜點店經驗佐證，最後提出看文字評論、偶爾嘗試評論少的店。要求都有回應，但影響的分析較淺，句型以簡單句與並列句為主，用字正確但平實。

top.comment_zh: 第一段以『一個數字決定兩家店的命運』切入，對照排隊與空店並歸納關鍵；第二段依『原因、影響（含評論越多客人越多的循環）、自己的做法』推進，有親身經驗（甜點店與鳳梨酥店），做法具體，結尾有見解。句型多變、用字精準，語言無誤。

steady.comment_zh: 回應所有要求，第一段對照清楚；第二段說明原因、影響與做法，也有經驗。對消費者與店家的影響寫得簡短，句型與用字偏基本（good、bad 重複）。語言無誤。
